newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares dip as some take profits.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares dip as some take profits.

text.p: Estonian shares dipped on Tuesday as some investors began to take profits from the recent bullish market trend, dealers said.
The Tallinn stock exchange index fell 0.36 percent to 197.16 and the official list turned over 63.4 million kroons.
"It seems that investors took their profits to prevent losses if the market turns down, although prices only dropped slightly," said one dealer.
Market leader Hansapank, who said earlier it would publish a 1997 profit forecast and last year's results on January 16, was again the most active share.
Hansapank also announced that it shares were now being traded on the over-the-counter market of the Munich bourse.
It turned over 30.4 million kroons to close 0.95 kroons lower at 185.05.
"The market is waiting for the Hansapank forecast because it is like a guiding post for further activity," said one trader.
Forekspank turned over 22.2 million kroons and closed 3.88 kroons higher at 142.78.
The bank yesterday forecast 1997 earnings of 75 million kroons.
Estonia's second bank, Savings Bank, turned over 4.5 million kroons and dropped 3.50 kroons to 88.50.
The over-the-counter market had volume of 12.8 million kroons. The Rakvere meat plant turned over 7.5 million kroons and closed at 16.45 kroons versus 15.90.
